### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.operators

### Question

I find that I frequently use `gmm` to duplicate a line only to then comment out the duplicated line, so I can make a slight variation of it. So, I thought I would use 'mini.operators' to build a `gmc` or `gC` mapping taking advantage of the `opts.multiply.func` to apply the comment string. Unfortunately, I'm not sure what I'm doing 😄 and could use assistance. My naive attempt that is not working:

```lua
Config.minioperators_comment_and_multiply = function(mode)
  local original_config = vim.b.minioperators_config
  vim.b.minioperators_config = {
    multiply = {
      func = function(content)
        return vim.tbl_map(function(line)
          local commentstring = vim.api.nvim_get_option_value("commentstring", { buf = 0 })
          local s, _ = string.gsub(commentstring, "%%s", line)
          return s
        end, content.lines)
      end,
    },
  }
  local result = MiniOperators.multiply(mode)
  vim.b.minioperators_config = original_config
  return result
end
```

And I try to bind it with:

```lua
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "gCC",  "<Cmd>lua Config.minioperators_comment_and_multiply('line')"),  "Duplicate and comment")
```

Thanks in advance.

comment_data.body:
Your approach is not that far off. I'd personally use local flag instead of buffer-local config.

So a more robust alternative is something like this:

```lua
local comment_multiply = false
local my_multiply_func = function(content)
  if not (comment_multiply and content.submode == 'V') then return content.lines end

  -- Add comment
  comment_multiply = false
  local commentstring = vim.bo.commentstring
  return vim.tbl_map(function(l) return (commentstring:gsub('%%s', l)) end, content.lines)
end
require('mini.operators').setup({ multiply = { func = my_multiply_func } })

local map_comment_multiply = function(mode, lhs, multiply_keys, desc)
  local rhs = function()
    -- Preserve cursor position so that it is on *not* commented part
    local pos = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)
    vim.schedule(function() vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, pos) end)

    comment_multiply = true
    return multiply_keys
  end

  local opts = { expr = true, remap = true, desc = desc }
  vim.keymap.set(mode, lhs, rhs, opts)
end

map_comment_multiply({ 'n', 'x' }, 'gC', 'gm', 'Multiply and comment')
map_comment_multiply('n', 'gCC', 'gmm', 'Multiply and comment line')
```

However, I'd personally use it only for a single line. In that case it is far easier (although doesn't preserve cursor):

```lua
vim.keymap.set('n', 'gCC', 'gmmgcck', { remap = true })
```

---

Also see #1806 and #730. I *am* thinking about maybe having `gcy` and `gcyy` in 'mini.comment' to do something like that ("yank and comment operator" and "yank and comment line"). This way the "multiply and comment" can be done like `gcy`-`p` or `gcy`-`P` or `gcyy`. The reason I did not like it before is because creating a mapping that starts with existing operator leads to certain subtle issues. The main one is that it implicitly occupies textobject mappings: a mapping like `gca` will conflict with using `gc` operator with `a` textobjects (like `ap`). But creating textobject that starts with either `y` / `d` / `c` is already a bad idea since it conflicts with built-in `yy` / `dd` / `cc`. So *maybe* having some "operator variants" that are essentially `<operator>` + `y`/`d`/`c` is not a bad idea.

Thank you and sorry I did not find those other posts. I actually did a search beforehand but I had limited it to the `operator` label. Doh.

In any case, you are right, 95% of the time I only need to do this for a single line, so your one-liner is appealing in that regard, but since you already wrote the version that supports blocks, so I can't let that go to waste, so it's been committed to my mini config 😄  Thanks!
